Lets take a step back for a second. 

Resume & Cover Letter Generator — Project Summary

What it does
I paste in a job posting. The system reads it, cross-references my entire work history and past cover letters, and produces a tailored resume and cover letter for that specific role — styled to match my existing InDesign design, not just as plain text.
It runs inside Claude Code as a set of slash commands (`/apply <folder-name>`) that chain together: analyze the posting → map my experience against it → draft the resume → draft the letter → audit both for accuracy. It pauses twice for your approval — once after mapping, so i see what's strong and what's missing before anything is written, and once after the audit, so you see every claim checked before you send anything.
What I am feeding it

* my current resume (2026 version), used to derive a strict formatting spec — exact conventions for dates, capitalization, bullet grammar, section order — plus my actual InDesign file (via IDML export) for fonts, colors, margins, and spacing, so generated output can be rendered pixel-close to my real design.
* Your entire work history, at a granularity that would produce roughly a 10-page master document — every role, project, metric, and story, fed in small batches so nothing gets embellished along the way.
* Past cover letters and writing samples (the writing samples come from 10 custom prompts designed to capture how i actually write, not interview-style answers), used to build a voice profile so generated letters sound like me rather than a generic competent stranger.

What comes out, per job application

* `resume_aaronallsop_"company name".pdf` — the designed version, full Pragmatica styling, matched to my current layout, capped at 2 pages
* `resume-ats_aaronallsop_"company name".docx` — a deliberately plain single-column version for portals that parse rather than read
* `cover-letter_aaronallsop_"company name".pdf` — same design system as the resume, under 350 words, matched styling (if I build the optional letter-PDF phase)
* Plus the intermediate files behind the scenes — the job analysis, the requirement mapping, and the audit report — so I can see exactly why the tailored version says what it says, and confirm every claim traces back to something real before you send it.
